author: Amara
text: The numerals argument feels like survivorship bias — we only know Hindu-Arabic numerals were the right answer because they won. A designer 'immersing themselves in the field' might have produced something equally good that we can't imagine now.

author: Julian
text: But that's kind of their point — the leap required mathematical insight, not design process. The counterfactual designer doesn't get there by interviewing tax collectors no matter how good they are.

author: Priya
text: This maps onto research tooling — the instruments that actually changed our lab came from people doing the research, not from vendors who interviewed us.

author: Theo
text: The Logo critique is harsher than it looks. If the test is 'do practitioners use it,' most educational tools fail. But maybe tools for learning a subject and tools for doing it are just different categories?

author: Amara
text: The floor/ceiling defense they dismiss actually deserves more credit — Scratch has a low ceiling too and it's still how a huge share of programmers started.

author: Nadia
text: Their own test cuts against them though — is the mnemonic medium used by serious practitioners, or is it Matuschak and Nielsen's Logo?
